subject: Aria Labs — Reserved capacity phasing & GPU price contingency
messages:
From: Tom Chan <tom.chan@arialabs.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Aria Labs — Reserved capacity phasing & GPU price contingency

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and infra about how Redwood would handle a multi-tranche reserved commitment tied to our expected Q3/Q4 usage growth:

- We want to phase the commitment (30% initial, +40% in Q3, +30% in Q4) — would that change the discount cadence?
- If GPU market costs spike (we're worried about supplier shortages), can you describe the price-protection constructs (floors/ceilings, indexation, credits) you offer?
- What approvals are required from Redwood to lock in a conditional discount tied to a pricing trigger?

Also, procurement needs an SOW/term sheet to circulate. Can you send a draft with the above options called out?

cc: procurement@arialabs.com

Thanks,
Tom Chan
Head of Procurement
Aria Labs
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>
To: Tom Chan <tom.chan@arialabs.com>
Cc: Aria Labs Procurement <procurement@arialabs.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Aria Labs — Reserved capacity phasing & GPU price contingency

Tom — thanks for the clear list. I put together a short draft SOW and three pricing guardrail options attached (aria_sow_draft.pdf). High level: 

Option A — Phased commit, locked unit price: 12-month term, staged capacity activation (30/40/30), 18% blended discount on reserved SKUs if Aria hits tranche milestones. No indexation; higher Redwood margin exposure.

Option B — Phased commit with price corridor: same staging, price floor at current index, price ceiling at +15% of today’s list. If market cost > ceiling, Redwood issues a one-time credit pro rata to months affected. Discount: 14% baseline, with +2% uplift when Q3 tranche activates.

Option C — Dynamic indexation: monthly adjustment tied to GPU index (we propose Redwood GPU Index v1). Discount starts at 16% but can move +/-3% based on index movements. Requires executive sign-off for downside > 10%.

Immediate asks from our side: usage profile by SKU (expected avg tokens/sec / concurrency), preferred billing cadence (monthly/quarterly), and whether Aria wants the credits as invoice credits or future commit top-ups.

I flagged the internal approval path in the draft; if you want, I can also propose a two-step sign-off (sales manager + finance) for indexation clauses.

Attachment: aria_sow_draft.pdf (SOW + pricing options)

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
Cc: Tom Chan <tom.chan@arialabs.com>, Aria Labs Procurement <procurement@arialabs.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Aria Labs — Reserved capacity phasing & GPU price contingency

Looping in Kim and outlining the internal ask: Aria is asking for a phasing-friendly reserved commit with a built-in protection if GPU market costs spike. For the external facing SOW we should recommend Option B (price corridor) as the default — balances predictability for Aria and protects Redwood from extreme volatility.

Operational details for internal review:
- Tranche activation rules: Aria provides 14-day ramp notice before each tranche activation.
- Burst capacity: allow 10% burst with pay-as-you-go pricing above the committed baseline.
- Monitoring: Redwood will provide token-level and GPU-util dashboards to certify tranche attainment.

Request to Finance: can we offer a 14% baseline discount with a +2% on tranche activation, and accept a credit-based remediation if index > ceiling? I don’t want to promise more than we can deliver without finance sign-off.

Thanks,
Karthik
From: michael_grant <michael_grant@redwood.example>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.example>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.example>
Date: 2027-05-02T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Aria Labs — Reserved capacity phasing & GPU price contingency

Confirming Finance position for the terms discussed. We ran a 24-month NPV on three scenarios (flat, +20% GPU cost spike, -10% GPU cost dip). Key takeaways:

- Floor/Ceiling corridor (Option B) is our preferred risk allocation. We can underwrite a ceiling of +15% above current cost for a one-time remediation credit.
- Pricing we can approve to commit to externally: 14% baseline discount on committed SKUs; +2% tranche activation uplift for each tranche after the first (so 14% -> 16% when Q3 tranche live).
- For indexation (Option C) we need Exec sign-off if the downside exposure on discount exceeds 8% over contract life.
- Approval path: Finance + Sales Manager (Kim) sign-off covers up to $4M incremental exposure. Anything beyond triggers CFO review.
- We prefer credits applied as invoice credits (simpler for revenue recognition) unless legal requires future commit top-ups.

I attached the pricing model used (pricing_model.xlsx) with scenario tabs.

Michael Grant
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing_model.xlsx

Tom — summarizing agreed path and next steps so your legal/procurement can circulate cleanly: 

1) Preferred structure: Option B (Phased commit with price corridor).
   - Baseline discount: 14% on reserved SKUs.
   - Tranche uplift: +2% when Q3 tranche activates (per Finance).
   - Price ceiling: +15% above current GPU index; if exceeded, Redwood issues pro-rata invoice credits for months affected.

2) Operational bullets: 14-day ramp notice; 10% burst above baseline billed at PAYG rates; monitoring via shared dashboards for tranche verification.

3) Approvals: Sales Manager (Kim) + Finance (Michael) have approved up to $4M exposure. Any exposure beyond that will route to CFO for review.

4) Next steps: I’ll upload the SOW + term sheet to the HubSpot deal and send a DocuSign link once you confirm SKU mix and billing cadence.
